title: add Python async RAG worker quickstart with local dev queue and streaming
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: provide a minimal, production-ish quickstart that demonstrates async worker-based RAG pipelines in Python using Redwood's streaming API and a lightweight local background queue. This quickstart targets engineers who want to offload long-running retrieval + generation cycles from web request threads, keep streaming to clients, and run locally with minimal infra. Included patterns: 1) async worker that pulls retrieval jobs from an in-memory queue (easy to swap for Redis/RQ or RabbitMQ), 2) incremental streaming to a WebSocket client via a small proxy server, 3) prefix caching for repeated queries, and 4) a SQLite-backed vector store shim for offline examples. What changed: added quickstart folder with a Python async worker example, dev Docker Compose for local run, a short doc page with architecture diagram (ASCII) and API examples, unit tests for core helpers, and CI job to smoke-test the local runner. Checklist: - [x] quickstart code + README - [x] Docker Compose for local dev - [x] smoke tests in CI - [x] docs page in /docs/quickstarts/ - [x] add links to SDK samples page - [x] initial performance notes and caveats (in README) High level commit summary and intent: - initial scaffolding and README describing goals and runbook - add async worker implementation (asyncio + aiohttp) with pluggable retrieval & storage interfaces - streaming proxy that relays tokens from Redwood API to WebSocket clients while worker completes retrieval and generation - convenience vectorstore using SQLite + ANN index (simple file-backed vector serialization) - lightweight test harness and CI job to run smoke test against local docker-compose Notes on productionization: this quickstart intentionally keeps infra minimal; for production teams we recommend swapping the in-memory queue for Redis or a cloud task queue, using a persistent vector DB (e.g., Milvus/Chroma), and enabling Redwood token-level tracing via the Console. The README documents tradeoffs and recommended next steps.

Maya Chen (author): Added retries and wait-for-health script in docker-compose; re-ran CI and it passed.
